title: Simulated embryonic regions take turns acting as the organizer

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simulated embryonic regions take turns acting as the organizer

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy between stripes first flows mainly from the red to the white stripe and then reverses, suggesting that the 'organizer' region (a group of cells that instructively patterns others) changes over time and embryonic regions take turns driving large-scale patterning.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The ‘organizer’ region (here defined as a region or group of cells in a tissue that can induce and instructively pattern other cells) seemed to change over time, suggesting embryonic regions take turns driving the large-scale process.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-10: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The directional reversal is a precise computational claim and the paper identifies public model code. Reproduction is feasible in weeks, although transfer entropy does not by itself establish instructive organizer activity.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun the published cellular automaton, calculate stripe-to-stripe transfer entropy over time, and test whether its signed direction changes from red-to-white to white-to-red. Failure of the reversal across the reported model and seeds would refute the simulation result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Results may depend on the selected evolved controller and estimator settings.

The organizer interpretation is stronger than the directional transfer-entropy result.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The information-theoretic contrast is specified tightly enough, and the model code is public, that recomputing stripe-to-stripe transfer entropy is analysis rather than a new experiment. What is missing is the evolved network and the traces behind the published peaks, so a re-evolution tests whether the reversal is a typical output, not whether the reported run had it. The organizer reading remains a gloss on that asymmetry.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On logged cell-state time series from the evolved French-flag network, compute pairwise local transfer entropy between red and white stripe cells with history k = 4, as defined in the paper. A red-to-white peak before about step 60 followed by a larger white-to-red peak confirms the reported reversal; no reversal, or a reversal that disappears under alternate binning, refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The published winner network and cell-state time series are not in the repository, and the committed run.py uses a two-generation demonstration setting.

Directed information flow is not a graft assay, so it does not show that a stripe instructively induces pattern in the other.

Transfer entropy is computed on one representative individual; stripe-to-stripe sums are confounded by which cells are actually changing state.

operationalizability: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.58
